title: Chapter 212: As Kind as the Sun
html:
Chen Ge stopped the workers and stepped forward. “Are you looking for me?”

Wang Hailong pushed through the crowd, drenched in sweat and gasping for breath. “My brother spoke last night! He’s outside the park and says he has something important to tell you!”

“Take me to him.” Just as Chen Ge had expected. After giving Uncle Xu brief instructions, he opened the Minghun scenario to visitors and left with Wang Hailong.

“I’m sorry to interrupt your business.” Wang Hailong wiped his forehead. “Shenglong has suffered so much. I couldn’t refuse him.”

“I understand.”

At the park entrance, a van waited across the street, its side painted with the words ‘Long Hu Fang’.

“He’s inside.” Wang Hailong led him toward the van. “You’ve seen my brother. He’s afraid his appearance will frighten people, so he didn’t want to be seen in public.”

Years spent resisting the thin monster had arrested Wang Shenglong’s emotional development. His mind remained childlike while his body grew grotesquely distorted. He rarely left his room and had become too large to climb onto a bed, forcing him to sleep on a thin mattress on the floor.

His situation reminded Chen Ge of The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

When Chen Ge first met Wang Shenglong at Hai Ming Apartments, the boy had drawn a picture of a monster perched on his shoulders, watching those around him as though ready to leap onto a new host.

The drawing had explained his torment. If he disobeyed, the monster would abandon him for another family member. To protect them, he bore the suffering alone and played its cruel game, remaining silent for five or six years.

Wang Hailong opened the rear doors, revealing a mountain-like silhouette deep inside. “Shenglong, I brought Boss Chen. Tell him whatever you need to say.”

The silhouette shifted forward, rocking the entire van.

“Don’t move. I’ll come inside.” Chen Ge and Wang Hailong climbed into the van and closed the doors. This was only Chen Ge’s second close encounter with Wang Shenglong. Folds of flesh obscured his age, and his body was impossibly broad.

“Wu…” Years of silence had made Wang Shenglong forget how to speak. He could form only the beginning of a sound, never the complete word.

“Don’t worry. Write down what you want to tell me.” At first, Chen Ge remained near the doors, ready to leap out at the first sign of danger. After observing Wang Shenglong, however, he saw a clear change: the stench surrounding him had vanished. Chen Ge passed him a notebook. Gripping the pen, Wang Shenglong wrote two words.

“I won.”

Two simple words, five or six years in the making. His refusal to say them had consumed his life. The pen nearly tore through the page, revealing the force of his excitement.

“Boss Chen, do you remember the story I told you?” Worried Chen Ge had missed the meaning, Wang Hailong leaned closer. “When my brother was young, a monster forced him into a game called ‘Who Speaks First.’ It lasted almost six years, but it seems my brother finally won.”

Then he whispered, “Boss Chen, my brother has only just recovered. Please humor him.”

Chen Ge glanced at Wang Hailong. The large man was gentler than his appearance suggested.

“Your brother truly is remarkable. I’ve met many people forced to play this game, and he is the only one who won.” Chen Ge clasped Wang Shenglong’s enormous hand. “You’re incredible.”

Wang Shenglong wrote again. “It only left temporarily. It said it would come back for me.”

“It will return?” A question occurred to Chen Ge as he read. “After spending almost six years tormenting you, why did it suddenly leave?”

“Something frightened it awake. It tried to seize my body by force, but failed. Then it left.”

“Frightened? By Doctor Gao and me?” Chen Ge pressed. “When did it awaken?”

“At 3 a.m. two days ago,” Wang Shenglong wrote. The date startled Chen Ge.

Two nights earlier, he had been livestreaming inside the Third Sick Hall. Did entering the world behind the door and awakening Men Nan’s primary personality also rouse the dormant monster?

Chen Ge considered the timing. The events were almost certainly connected, though that could not be the whole explanation.

“That night, when the monster left, did you see or hear anything out of place?”

“There was the sound of people walking backwards in the corridor.”

“Walking backwards?”

Wang Shenglong filled the page with an explanation, but Chen Ge still could not understand. Frustration brought sweat pouring from him.

“It’s all right. That clue is enough.” Chen Ge could not imagine how backward footsteps differed from ordinary ones. In front of the brothers, he called Captain Yan.

“Captain Yan, I received new information about the Third Sick Hall. One of the escaped patients may have appeared at Hai Ming Apartments.” The creature attached to Wang Shenglong had come through the Third Sick Hall’s door, then broken away from the others. Only another monster from the same place was likely to frighten it into fleeing.

Such creatures needed living hosts to remain outside for long. The backward footsteps Wang Shenglong heard probably belonged to one of the Third Sick Hall patients.

Wang Hailong had assumed Chen Ge was merely humoring his brother. When he called the police, panic set in. “What’s happening? Why did you call them?”

Only then did he grasp the situation’s gravity: Chen Ge had never been joking.

“Boss Chen, what have you been talking about? The police are coming to Hai Ming Apartments?” Wang Hailong’s face was filled with worry.

“Your brother’s story is connected to another case. That’s all I can tell you.” Chen Ge spoke with Wang Shenglong a little longer, then left the van.

Worried, Wang Hailong followed. “Boss Chen, my brother has spent his whole life at home. He has never done anything illegal.”

“I know. More precisely, the case concerns the monster from his story.”

“The monster?” Wang Hailong’s expression changed. After a long silence, he asked, “Will this affect my brother? He has suffered enough, and it took so long for him to speak again.”

“Don’t worry. Your brother will be fine.” Chen Ge looked into the van. Wang Shenglong sat like a small mountain in the corner, hidden where sunlight could not reach. He clutched the pen and appeared to be drawing.
